79865.subject: Revenue Doesn't Matter
79865.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

As we crawl out of what has been a brutal bear market, we find in front of us an optimistic and seemingly more mature crypto market environment. Following the example of HYPE, a pure, pristine asset gifted from Jeff to the people against a backdrop of low-float, high-FDV insider plays (remember TIA?), momentum and outperformance have shifted toward quality assets with high-quality tokenomics and revenue-generating businesses.

But is this really the case? Are we valuing tokens like equities, on the future cash flows they produce, or is this just another meta?

At its core, revenue investing underwrites one of two things: existing earnings power (value) or future earnings power (growth). In the first case, current or trailing cash flows justify the price with limited growth assumptions. In the second, the bet is that those cash flows, or the opportunity set around them, will expand beyond what the current price implies.

On the first point, "value" is the wrong framework for investing in crypto tokens. While P/S is commonly used as a metric, what it is really saying is: this asset is valued at X years of current revenue. In discounted cash flow terms, the buyer believes future revenue, discounted at the return that the risk of the business demands, is worth at least that price; with flat revenue, that price implies a yearly return of 1/X, and growth adds to it. This can be "cheap" and a valid reason to invest in the equities of traditional companies, whose revenue persists, but crypto is so cyclical and volatile, with so much leader churn, that through this lens even "cheap" protocols look expensive.

For example, launchpads are often pushed as cheap at a median 5.7x FDV to revenue, yet a year after its peak week the median launchpad earns 0.3% of that week's revenue (1.3% at the 75th percentile). Measured on a peak quarter, 5.7 years of current revenue is closer to 29 years of what launchpads actually go on to earn.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0d730b78-b1e2-4bdc-a937-b2e36d2540b8/image.png?t=1790598212)
Caption: 

This is not limited to launchpads. Of 119 protocols and chains that earned $5M+ in a quarter and peaked at least a year ago, the median now earns 5% of its peak, and 62% are down more than 90%. With the median asset far too volatile and uncertain to be invested due to value, we consider the next reason: growth.
